learningObjectives.text: Identify the central source-grounded idea in Jason and Medea.
Connect the idea to the cited source, genre, and version.

argo.author: Apollonius Rhodius
argo.excerpt: Beginning with thee, O Phoebus, I will recount the famous deeds of men of old, who, at the behest of King Pelias, down through the mouth of Pontus and between the Cyanean rocks, sped well-benched Argo in quest of the golden fleece. Such was the oracle that Pelias heard, that a hateful doom awaited him
argo.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

medea.author: Euripides

medea.excerpt: and there marries Ægeus son of Pandion. * * * * * MEDEA. * * * * NURSE OF MEDEA. Would that the hull of Argo had not winged her way to the Colchian land through the Cyanean Symplegades,[1] and that the pine felled in the forests of Pelion had never fallen, nor had caused the hands of the chiefs to row,[2]

narrativeBlocks.title: A quest story
narrativeBlocks.body: The Argonautica presents Jason through the voyage of the Argo and the community of heroes around it.

narrativeBlocks.title: Genre changes the question
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotations are available under the source buttons. They are translations, not the lesson author’s wording. Compare the work and locator before drawing conclusions.

narrativeBlocks.title: Ask what genre does
narrativeBlocks.body: An epic quest and a tragic play can preserve the same names while asking different questions about loyalty and blame.

narrativeBlocks.title: Follow who supplies the means
narrativeBlocks.body: The quest cannot be understood only through Jason’s title. Watch where crucial knowledge, help, and dangerous choices come from—especially when later sources shift the blame.

narrativeBlocks.title: Epic success becomes tragic evidence
narrativeBlocks.body: The Argonautica makes the voyage famous; Euripides turns the same voyage into a reason for catastrophe. Holding both versions together prevents “the quest” from becoming a neutral legend.

quiz.prompt: Who supplies essential help to Jason?
quiz.explanation: Medea. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: How do the Argonautica and Medea differ?

choices.text: Both are victory odes for Pelias.
Epic narrates the quest; tragedy stages a later crisis.
Both are the same author’s diary.
